judgments.reasoning_cat1: A structured consent-condition with a numerical threshold; the only softness is 'as soon as practicable' and the Insurer's 'sole discretion'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Mergers Endorsement (c179) deletes and replaces this subsection with a 20% threshold rather than 25%, and the Discovery Period endorsement deletes Section XII altogether (c006), so three documents give three answers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short automatic-coverage grant keyed to a numerical asset test; definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is replaced by c180 (20% instead of 25%) and is the very provision the Company definition (c042) makes itself 'subject to', while c006 deletes Section XII entirely for the Discovery Period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out for anything 'arising out of or directly or indirectly resulting from' pre-acquisition Wrongful Acts is very wide, and limb (2) depends on the loose Interrelated Wrongful Acts test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section V(O) (c077) excepts claims 'as provided in Section XII (C)(3)', but this subsection has only limbs (1) and (2); and c181 preserves 'all other provisions of Section XII' while c006 deletes them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three sentences on return premium are hard to reconcile with each other: a flat 90% rule, then a 90% rule for multi-year policies before the first anniversary, then pro rata afterwards, with no rule for a multi-year policy in year one that is not covered by the second sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 10(b) shows three-year pre-paid premiums, so the multi-year branch is live, and the Discovery Period fully-earned rules (c007, c037) and c106(2) further restrict cancellation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear notice mechanics with two defined notice periods; nothing intrinsically uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Iowa Amendatory Endorsement (c187) deletes and replaces this very subsection with a different and longer scheme, so the printed text is superseded but still appears in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the Company ceasing to engage actively in its primary business' is a vague trigger for cutting off coverage, and 'acquisition of substantially all of the assets' imports another elastic standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (2) preserves the Discovery Period right on the occurrence of ANY of the three conversion events, but Section III (c037) confers that right only where the Policy converts 'subject to Section XIII (C)(1)(b)' — a direct inconsistency that matters where Financial Impairment under (C)(1)(a) occurs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allocation 'based on the relative legal exposures of the parties' is a standard whose application is inherently contestable, and limb (1)(a) deems 100% of joint non-defence Loss to be the Insured Persons' while (1)(b) allocates 'all other Loss', which is hard to square.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the arbitration machinery in c108 and the retention rules in c091, but the 100% deeming in (1)(a) pulls against the Insurer's 100% payment obligation in c091(B)(4) and the order of payments in c094.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Arbitration is available only 'if requested by the Insured' and only for Defense Costs allocation, and the Insurer need advance only what it 'believes to be covered' — permissive and self-judging language of the kind courts have had to parse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The advancement standard here is weaker than the unqualified advancement duty in c096(1), which is expressly made 'Subject to Section XIV', so the two provisions must be read together to know what is actually owed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (1) says the Application is construed as a separate application by each Insured Person while limb (2) says the Policy is not a series of individual contracts — two statements pulling in opposite directions within one clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That tension carries into the Severability provisions (c110, c111), which sever knowledge person by person yet deny coverage to the Company on senior officers' knowledge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limbs (1)-(3) key rescission to who 'knew' of undisclosed facts, but the closing sentence says the conditions apply 'whether or not the Insured Person actually knew if the misrepresentation ... was made' — a sentence that both is garbled and appears to undo the knowledge requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the Severability of Exclusions provision (c111), which forbids imputing one Insured Person's knowledge to another, and against c109(1)'s separate-application rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The non-imputation rule in (1) is stated absolutely and then (2) imputes senior officers' knowledge to the Company for two exclusions only, an expressio unius structure with real bite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its non-imputation principle is difficult to reconcile with the final sentence of the Severability clause (c110) and with c109(2)'s denial that the Policy is a set of individual contracts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional subrogation clause with broad cooperation language; nothing genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside the excess/other insurance clause (c118) and the Insured vs. Insured Exclusion (c072) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The entire-agreement recital lists 'this Policy, the Application, and any written Endorsements' but not the Declarations, and the anti-assignment sentence is bolted on without connection.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The constituent-document statements in c018 and the 'Policy' definition (c054) list different sets, so the integration clause does not match either exactly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Automatic conformity to 'any applicable laws governing this Policy' is stated in the broadest possible terms without identifying the governing law.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Iowa Amendatory Endorsement (c186, c187) does the same job expressly for one subsection, which raises the question of what work this general clause still does.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad agency appointment with an illustrative but non-exhaustive list ('including, but not limited to'); the residual scope of the agency is not fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because the Named Insured changed when Item 1 was amended (c025, read with c053), who holds this authority shifted mid-term, which matters for cancellation and Discovery Period election under c037 and c104.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear no-waiver/no-oral-modification clause; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the entire-agreement clause (c113) and the endorsement non-variation clauses (c009, c023).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'full compliance with all the terms of this Policy' as a condition precedent to any action is absolute language that courts often have to soften, and requiring the claimant's written agreement makes the alternative route near-impossible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It compounds the conditions precedent scattered elsewhere (c097, c098, c100), any breach of which would on this wording bar suit entirely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening sentence ('shall not be subject to the terms of any other insurance') and the following excess-of-all-other-insurance rule sit awkwardly together, and 'regardless of whether collectable' is a striking one-sided term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The not-for-profit coverage in c036 is also made excess over other insurance, and the Prohibition on Stacking provisions (c121, c175) address overlapping ground by a different mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short administrative undertaking with a fixed ten-day period; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on the Loss Information definition (c052); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite statement that Financial Impairment neither releases the Insurer nor deprives it of rights.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is hard to reconcile with the Insolvency Exclusion (c083), which excludes Loss 'in any way involving the Financial Impairment of the Company', and it bears on whether the Insured vs. Insured Exclusion (c072) can bar a receiver's claim.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the largest available Limit of Liability under this Policy or any other policy issued by the Insurer' is an odd formulation that can be read as a cap or as an entitlement, and the self-describing 'this paragraph creates a sublimit' does not resolve it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Securities Liability Endorsement (c175) deletes and replaces this very subsection and adds a further anti-overlap sentence, so the printed version is superseded but remains in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear statement that headings are of no effect; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Numerous provisions identify others by their headings — c130, c147, c154, c167, c175 and c186 all delete or amend subsections 'entitled' something — which sits uneasily with headings forming no part of the terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare amending preamble; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other endorsement preambles; the substantive change is in c124.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad securities exclusion followed by a carve-back identified only by a form number ('the Securities Liability Insuring Agreement, Form 5098'), so the exclusion's practical reach depends on an external document reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts across Item 6's note that Insuring Agreement (C) 'includes coverage for ... Securities Liability' (c015) and must be read with the Securities Liability grant (c165) and the anti-overlap sentence in c175.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare effective date; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Policy inception; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard non-variation boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Self-limiting against the exclusion it accompanies; mirrors the other endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare preamble; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c144 and c164.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant runs to 'the Insured' — which includes the Company and every Insured Person — for Wrongful Acts 'in rendering or failing to render' Brokerage/Advisory Services, importing the elastic definition in c039.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It only works because c131 deletes the Section V(B) exclusion (c064) for this endorsement, and Section IV's Wrongful Act definition (c061(3)) limits entity coverage to what an Insuring Agreement grants — a chain that must be assembled across documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short lead-in to a list of variations; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'all of the terms and conditions ... shall apply except' formula raises the usual question of how endorsement-specific variations interact with the base form, but nothing specific conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line deletion of a named subsection; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section II(B) is deleted for this coverage only, and separately for the Fiduciary and Securities coverages (c147, c167), so c036 survives only for the D&O and Broad Form coverages — coherent but fragmented.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite instruction applying Section V except one named subsection.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It leaves the Insured vs. Insured Exclusion (c072) and other Section V exclusions applying to Brokerage claims, which is a substantial and non-obvious carry-over into a professional liability coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite exclusion identifying a class of barred claimants.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates c080, c156 and c169 word for word, so the same exclusion sits in four places under different coverages.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short fee-dispute exclusion; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'the Company's services' although this endorsement's coverage runs to the Insured generally, and it overlaps the Loss carve-out in c051(7).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The counterfactual carve-back ('unless such liability would be imposed regardless') is genuinely difficult to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c081, c157 and c170; overlaps c051(5) but does not contradict it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso applies 'solely in connection with an Insured's investment on behalf of a customer in the stock of' entities in limbs (2) and (3) — pointedly not limb (1) — which is a narrow and easily contested carve-back.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It differs from the otherwise identical exclusions in c083 and c172 by adding this proviso, and from c159, which omits the Financial Impairment limb altogether, so the same exclusion has four different scopes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated categories with a limited 'like services' tail; the missing colon after 'providing' is a harmless scan artefact.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c084; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Closes with 'any other investment banking activity' — a bare catch-all after five specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c085 and c173; the parenthetical exception for the Company's own securities keeps it consistent with c165.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'actual or written representations, promises or guarantees' is almost certainly a mis-rendering of 'oral or written', and as written the phrase has no coherent meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has no counterpart elsewhere in the instrument, so nothing else resolves the wording.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific mechanical/electronic failure exclusion; tightly bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing provision; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three named capacities; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c088 and c174; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short statutory exclusion; its reach to 'violations of' RICO is definite enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It appears only in this endorsement, so RICO claims are excluded for Brokerage but not for the other coverages — an asymmetry that must be read against c069 and c070.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare effective date; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Policy inception date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard non-variation boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Self-limiting; mirrors the other endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare preamble; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c127 and c164.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant reaches Wrongful Acts 'resulting from the Administration of any Employee Benefit Plan or the violation of any of the responsibilities ... imposed by ERISA ... or any common law or statutory law relating to any Employee Benefit Plan' — a very wide closing catch-all attached to specific triggers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It only operates because c154 deletes the ERISA Exclusion (c067) for this endorsement, while the Employment Practices Exclusion (c066) and c160 continue to bite on adjacent ground.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short lead-in; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same structure as c129 and c166; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line deletion of a named subsection; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to c130 and c167; leaves c036 alive only for some coverages.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'counseling Employees with respect to, interpreting, handling records in connection with, or effecting enrollment or cancellation' is a closed list, but the omission of general plan administration makes its boundary against the Insuring Agreement contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines the scope of both the grant (c145) and the added Insured vs. Insured carve-out (c155(4)), so a narrow reading shrinks both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'operated solely by the Company or jointly by the Company and a labor organization' is a restrictive formula whose application to multi-employer or successor plans is not obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds the replaced Insured definition (c152), which sweeps in plans 'existing before the Policy Period' and plans acquired 'pursuant to Section XII' — a section deleted for the Discovery Period by c006.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tracks the ERISA statutory formula closely, including 'or as a result of surrounding circumstances', which is broad but borrowed language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c149 and c151; no conflict found.
